messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finchai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - post-call recap & next steps

Alex - great to meet today. Quick recap from our call + a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a Dedicated capacity proposal:

Summary of what I heard:
- Monthly token volume: ~800M tokens/month (average), with spikes up to ~1.2B tokens in high-usage months.
- Target unit economics: looking for ~$200 per 1M tokens (target cost of goods).
- Preferred GPU: leaning toward H100 (80GB) for multi-model and larger context support, but open to A100 (40GB) if that hits budget.
- Desired reserved capacity: starting point: 6x-8x GPUs reserved, with autoscale/burst up to 10 during peaks.
- Throughput targets: baseline sustained throughput ~3k tokens/sec; peak sustained windows up to ~12k tokens/sec; p95 latency target for generation paths ~300-500ms for typical prompts.
- Timing: procurement / PO expected within 6-8 weeks.

Open questions for you (please confirm by EOD Monday if possible):
1) Can you confirm the 800M monthly average and whether that includes embeddings traffic (yes/no)? Embeddings would change the unit economics.
2) Any hard constraints on GPU type (H100 only) or is A100 acceptable for a lower cost option?
3) Do you have a preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. annual commit)?

Attached: proposed_capacity_breakdown.xlsx (high level throughput / GPU mapping) and our mutual_action_plan.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
- We'll run a quick internal sizing/pricing pass (Marcus + Vanessa) and send a ballpark cost estimate by Wed, Mar 25.
- Follow-up pricing call with you and procurement the week of Mar 30 to align on SOW and discounts.

Thanks - enjoy the weekend.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finchai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finchai.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinchAI

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap and the clear asks. Confirming:
- 800M/mo average is correct and includes ~100M/month of embedding tokens (we're primarily generation workload, embeddings are a smaller fraction).
- We prefer H100 for the memory headroom (several of our models are 65B+ and we want consistent performance). A100 would be acceptable only if it meaningfully improves pricing.
- Billing: prefer annual commit if it helps with unit cost, but can consider monthly for the first 2-3 months during ramp.

A couple of clarifications on throughput: our internal analytics show baseline concurrent sessions ~120 active users during business hours, with bursts up to ~600 concurrent users for a 15-30 minute window during marketing sends. Peak token/sec of ~12k matches our estimates - would want to maintain p95 inference latency <500ms.

Procurement note: we need a ballpark TCO (monthly) to present to finance this week. They asked for a target $/1M tokens number and a comparison: dedicated reserved setup vs. hosted-exchange rates. Our internal target is $180-220 per 1M tokens (ideally closer to $180). If you can run a scenario for 6xH100 reserved vs 8xH100 reserved (with autoscale to 10) that would be helpful.

I'm looping procurement on this thread (procurement@finchai.com). We can also share a draft SOW if helpful - I'll upload it to the shared link and send it over.

--
Alex Jones | Head of Platform, FinchAI
alex.jones@finchai.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finchai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@finchai.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinchAI

Thanks Alex - perfect, that helps. Quick response / plan:

1) We'll run a pricing scenario for:
   - 6x H100 reserved (baseline) with autoscale to 8 for normal peaks
   - 8x H100 reserved with autoscale to 10 for high-growth scenario
   - For each scenario we'll give: monthly reserved cost, estimated token throughput per GPU (tokens/sec), and an implied $/1M tokens figure using your 800M/mo baseline and 100M embeddings split.

2) Early unit economics (very rough):
   - Estimated average throughput per H100: ~2.5k tokens/sec for mixed-generation workloads (this depends on model family & prompt length).
   - With 6xH100 baseline that maps to ~15k tokens/sec peak capacity (with autoscale buffers) - should cover your stated peaks if workloads are evenly balanced across GPUs; longer contexts or larger models reduce per-GPU throughput.
   - Ballpark pricing: with an annual commit we can approach an effective $/1M tokens in the $165-210 range depending on final GPU count and burst/overage terms. Monthly commit will be higher - we'll show both.

3) Action items: Vanessa / Marcus - can you run the two scenarios and a concise slide (1-2 pages) showing: reserved monthly cost, implied $/1M tokens, and assumptions (model family, avg prompt length, embedding cost). I attached the capacity breakdown for reference.

4) Alex / procurement - if you can share the draft SOW or procurement timelines by Tue EOD we'll incorporate into the commercial terms.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a pricing review on Wed, Mar 25 at 11am PT unless you prefer a different time.

--
Marissa

- Account: FinchAI (deal RWI-202603-AI-2345)
- Confirmed volumes: 800M tokens/mo (100M embeddings)
- Preferred GPU: H100 80GB; scenarios requested: 6xH100 (autoscale to 8) and 8xH100 (autoscale to 10)
- Target $/1M tokens from customer: $180-220 (they prefer ~$180)
- Throughput targets: baseline ~3k tokens/sec; peaks ~12k tokens/sec; p95 latency <500ms

Please prepare:

- Suggested discount bands for annual vs monthly commit.

Timeline: need the slide + numbers by Wed Mar 25 EOD so Marissa can send ballpark to customer and schedule the pricing call for Mar 30.

Thanks - Marissa
